title: New Robot Butler Can Help You Find Your Keys
paragraphs: Imagine if you could have your own personal assistant — someone to keep your home tidy, bring you cups of coffee and remind you where you left your keys. Wouldn't that be nice?
Well, that's exactly what Tuesday Labs, a robotics company in New York, is offering with its newest creation: Voxel.

Voxel, which Tuesday Labs describes as a "droid butler," is designed to perform daily tasks around the house. A video released by the company shows the robot sweeping up crumbs, watering plants, bringing its owner a musical instrument — and even dancing along to the music!
Voxel can also help you find things. If you can't find your keys, for example, ask Voxel, and it will tell you where it last saw them.

Rosalind Shinkle, CEO of Tuesday Labs, told design magazine Dezeen that part of her reason for creating Voxel was because she hates cleaning! However, she also wanted to build a robot that would be nice to live with.
Robots that look too much like humans can feel a little creepy, so Tuesday Labs worked with a former character designer from Pixar to create a friendly-looking robot that doesn't look human at all.

Instead of having a head, Voxel has a simple face on its body — two animated eyes above a line for a mouth. Its body is covered in a colorful and lightweight plastic shell, and hidden cameras allow it to find its way around the home.
Voxel stands about as tall as a kitchen counter, but its legs allow it to adjust its height to reach tables and shelves.
Tuesday Labs plans to start delivering Voxel in 2028, and the robot is expected to cost around $20,000. However, the company hopes to make more affordable robots in the future.
